bull_bear.body:
- Largest pan-India multispecialty hospital network by bed capacity and second largest by number of hospitals (Sep 30, 2025)
- Only private hospital chain leading in three metros - Bengaluru, Kolkata and Pune - by bed capacity
- Widest hospital footprint among private hospital chains in India across 14 states and union territories
- Balanced metro / non-metro presence (~42.72% beds in metros, ~57.28% in non-metros)
- High-acuity CONGO-R specialty mix (~60-64% of gross inpatient revenue) supporting revenue quality
- Highest revenue growth and among the highest EBITDA margin and ROCE among major hospital players (FY2023-FY2025, CRISIL)
- Track record of value-accretive acquisitions and post-acquisition margin improvement
- Backing of Promoters and global institutional investors (Temasek, TPG, Novo Holdings)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic concentration in Karnataka — Karnataka hospitals contributed 51.55% of FY2025 revenue (66.61% in FY2023); disruption or policy change there would materially hurt results
- Acquisition integration risk — Growth relies heavily on acquisitions (AMRI, Medica Synergie, Sahyadri); failure to integrate/upgrade could erode expected synergies
- Reliance on pro forma financials — Pro forma information reflecting the Acquisition Transactions may not be indicative of actual or future results
- O&M / managed-hospital agreement risk — Six O&M hospitals operated under trust agreements (HCMCT, EIHF, KMMMT) carry contractual continuation risk
- Payor mix dependence on insurance/TPA and government — ~49% of revenue from insurance/TPA and ~13% from government schemes exposes pricing to third-party and regulatory pressure
- Execution risk on bed-expansion plans — Planned ~751 brownfield and ~1,943 greenfield beds by 2030 depend on capex, approvals and ramp-up timelines
- Regulatory and accreditation dependence — Business depends on licensed-bed approvals and NABH/NABL accreditations that can be withdrawn or delayed

outlook.body: Manipal plans to add approximately 751 licensed beds across existing hospitals and approximately 1,943 licensed beds through greenfield projects by 2030 to support growth. Its network grew from 28 hospitals with 7,699 licensed beds (Mar 31, 2023) to 48 hospitals with 12,367 licensed beds (pro forma, Sep 30, 2025), aided by acquisitions of AMRI (Sep 2023), Medica Synergie (Jul 2024) and Sahyadri (Oct 2025, adding 1,606 beds). - Occupancy and operational-bed ramp of acquired/upgraded hospitals
- Post-acquisition margin improvement (e.g. Columbia Asia EBITDA margin 27.41% to 31.95%)
- Material cost to revenue held stable around ~20%

internal_operational.detail: A substantial number of hospitals and revenue are concentrated in Karnataka; any loss of business, disruption, disease outbreak, or state policy/geopolitical change there could materially hurt operations. As of Sept 30, 2025, 18 of 48 hospitals with 6,040 of 12,367 licensed beds were in Karnataka.
internal_operational.evidence: Karnataka contributed 49.55%, 51.55%, 59.98% and 66.61% of revenue from operations in H1 FY26 and FY2025/2024/2023; Karnataka revenue Rs 23,353.83M (49.55%) H1 FY26 vs total Rs 47,130.53M; new 264-bed Karnataka hospital opened Nov 2025.
internal_operational.title: Geographic concentration in Karnataka

internal_operational.detail: Revenue is primarily generated from inpatient care, so inconsistent or declining patient volumes/occupancy would hurt profitability given high fixed costs; ramp-up of new/expanded facilities may take longer than expected.
internal_operational.evidence: Inpatient volume 288,260 (H1 FY26 pro forma)/237,388; occupancy 65.11%/65.31% H1 FY26, 66.19%/67.09% FY25, 65.32% FY24, 63.47% FY23; revenue from operations Rs 53,129.20M H1 FY26 pro forma.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on inpatient admissions and occupancy

internal_operational.detail: Significant revenue is derived from six specialties (cardiac, oncology, neuro, gastro, orthopaedics, renal). Negative demand shifts, loss of preferred doctors, alternative treatments or competition in these specialties could adversely impact results and limit ability to diversify.
internal_operational.evidence: CONGO-R = 64.08%, 62.56%, 61.55%, 60.25% of gross inpatient revenue in H1 FY26 and FY25/24/23; CONGO-R revenue Rs 25,793.64M vs gross inpatient revenue Rs 40,513.22M (63.68%) H1 FY26 pro forma.
internal_operational.title: Specialty concentration in CONGO-R

internal_operational.detail: The 'Manipal Hospitals' brand is critical; negligence, malpractice, mortality, regulator action or media/social-media negative publicity (regardless of accuracy) could erode trust and market recognition and raise marketing costs.
internal_operational.evidence: Negative publicity cited re: former Manipal Hospital Jaipur doctor/transplant-coordinator organ-transplant investigation and Sahyadri Acquisition notices from Collector of Stamps/PMC to KMMMT over Deccan Gymkhana land (99-year PMC lease to KMMMT).
internal_operational.title: Failure to maintain and enhance brand/reputation and negative publicity

internal_operational.detail: Operations depend on scarce, highly competitive healthcare professionals; attrition raises recruitment/training costs, reduces productivity and could raise compensation, especially given up to 10-year specialist training periods and 2-year consultant terms.
internal_operational.evidence: As of Sept 30, 2025 (pro forma): 11,058 doctors (8,229 consultancy/fee-for-service, 2,170 junior, 659 DNB/fellowship), 9,670 nurses, 5,254 paramedics, 370 senior hospital mgmt; H1 FY26 attrition: doctors 6.85%, nurses 10.06%, paramedics 9.46%, senior mgmt 5.95%.
internal_operational.title: Retention/attraction of doctors, nurses and senior hospital management

internal_operational.detail: Performance depends on MD & CEO Dilip Jose Puthiyidathu, CFO Sameer Agarwal, COO Karthik Rajagopal and other key personnel; inability to attract/retain scarce industry-specific talent could adversely affect the business.
internal_operational.evidence: DRHP states no KMP/Senior Management attrition experienced across H1 FY26 and FY2025/2024/2023.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on Key Management Personnel and Senior Management

internal_operational.detail: Dependence on third parties for medical consumables/pharmacy items, equipment, housekeeping and security exposes the company to supply-chain bottlenecks, quality issues, equipment discontinuation and inability to pass through cost increases; limited number of equipment suppliers and authorized service providers.
internal_operational.evidence: Medical consumables & pharmacy purchases + inventory change Rs 9,654.34M H1 FY26 (23.93% of total expenses), Rs 16,800.36M FY25; housekeeping Rs 1,052.88M (2.61%); security Rs 318.94M (0.79%). Geopolitical (Middle East, Russia-Ukraine) supply-chain exposure noted.
internal_operational.title: Reliance on third-party suppliers, subcontractors and service providers

internal_operational.detail: Failure to keep pace with technological change, evolving standards and patient needs, or obsolescence/malfunction of equipment (including AI, hospital information system, ambulances) could impair services, cause impairment charges and reduce market share.
internal_operational.evidence: Company embeds AI in marketing, telehealth, diagnostics, call-centre and e-pharmacy prescription reading; imports certain equipment (currency risk); relies on hospital information system across network.
internal_operational.title: Technological change and equipment obsolescence

internal_operational.detail: Non-100% ownership in several subsidiaries/step-down subsidiaries and reliance on trust-based JV/O&M/PPP arrangements (three-year terms, terminable) mean deterioration in stakeholder relationships could disrupt hospital management and operations.
internal_operational.evidence: Non-wholly-owned entities include MH (East) India, Sahyadri Hospitals, Saideep Healthcare, Surya Hospitals, Sahyadri Karad, Manipal Hospitals Bengal, MHSPL and HealthMap; 3 hospitals run via JV/concession/MoU with HCMCT, EIHF, KMMMT; six O&M hospitals.
internal_operational.title: Reliance on relationships with group partners and stakeholders

internal_operational.detail: Six hospitals are operated under O&M agreements terminable by counterparties MAHE and Sikkim Manipal University if targets are not met; failure to renew on acceptable terms or termination could hurt results.
internal_operational.evidence: O&M hospitals revenue Rs 265.45M (0.50%) H1 FY26 pro forma, Rs 425.75M (0.46%) FY25 pro forma; owned hospitals Rs 52,863.75M (99.50%).
internal_operational.title: Risks from O&M (operation and management) hospital agreements

internal_operational.detail: Efficient operation depends on IT infrastructure (hospital management system, ERP); interruptions, breaches, ransomware, phishing or data leaks could disrupt patient care, corrupt clinical/financial data and cause loss of sensitive personal information.
internal_operational.evidence: Example: CCTV cameras at Manipal Hospital Vijayawada were hacked with a ransom demand (cyber complaint filed, matter closed). Company maintains cybersecurity insurance.
internal_operational.title: IT systems failure and cybersecurity risk

internal_operational.detail: Manpower-intensive operations and stringent Indian labour law expose the company to union action, strikes and work stoppages that could disrupt operations and raise costs.
internal_operational.evidence: As of Sept 30, 2025, 1,355 employees at five hospitals are union members.
internal_operational.title: Labour unrest, slowdowns and work stoppages

internal_operational.detail: Storage and use of flammable chemicals (alcohol, sanitizers, gases, fuel) exposes hospitals to fire/explosion risk; Tower I of KMC Hospital Mangalore predates NBC 2016 and cannot obtain a fire license.
internal_operational.evidence: Company complies with periodic fire-safety advisories for KMC Mangalore Tower I; no significant fire instances in H1 FY26 or last three Fiscals.
internal_operational.title: Use of highly flammable/explosive materials and fire risk

internal_operational.detail: As operations scale, inadequacy or failure of internal processes/systems, human error, or fraud/whistleblower investigations could impair financial reporting, invite investor confidence loss and anti-bribery/anti-corruption penalties.
internal_operational.evidence: DRHP notes high transaction volumes where errors may be repeated/compounded; whistleblower policy and code of conduct in place.
internal_operational.title: Inability to establish/maintain effective internal controls

internal_operational.detail: Aging owned hospitals require rising refurbishment/renovation spend that may reduce usable premises and operating capacity; for O&M hospitals the company can be indirectly affected through reduced capacity.
internal_operational.evidence: No quantified figures disclosed in this risk factor.
internal_operational.title: Repair, maintenance, physical damage or renovation disruption

internal_operational.detail: Events beyond the company's control could cause economic instability, impair facilities and increase costs; infectious-disease outbreaks could diminish public trust in hospitals.
internal_operational.evidence: West Bengal hospitals impacted by Cyclone Amphan (2020); Manipal Hospital Dhakuria basement flooded Sept 22, 2025, decommissioning certain radiation equipment and temporary basement sealing.
internal_operational.title: Natural disasters, fires, epidemics, pandemics, war, terrorism, civil unrest
